50. (New) A removable cargo bay support system for a cargo aircraft, comprising:at least one rail disposed in an interior cargo bay of a cargo aircraft, the interior cargo bay having a forward bay portion located in a forward end of the cargo aircraft, an aft bay portion located in an aft end of the cargo aircraft, and the at least one rail extending longitudinally along a length of the forward bay portion and a length of the aft bay portion, the interior cargo bay defining a nominal width and a constricted width along the at least one rail, the constricted width being less than the nominal width and less than a width of the interior cargo bay along the at least one rail forward and aft of a location of the constricted width; andat least one cargo support segment configured to be removeably attached to the at least one rail, and, when attached to the at least one rail, the at least one cargo support segment is transformable between a first arrangement in which the at least one cargo support segment is translatable along a length of the at least one rail, and a second arrangement in which the at least one cargo support segment is fixedly secured with respect to a location along the length of the at least one rail,SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.080.05
wherein the at least one cargo support segment comprises a fixed central region and opposing lateral end segments moveably coupled to the fixed region and moveable between a first position and a second position, the first position defining a first width of the at least one cargo support segment that is less than the constricted width and the second position defining a second width of the at least one cargo support segment that is less than the nominal width and greater than the constricted width.
51. (New) The system of The system of wherein the at least one cargo support segment is configured to support cargo weight and direct at least a majority of the cargo weight supported by the at least one cargo support segment into the at least one rail, and
wherein the opposing lateral end segments are configured to, in the second position,
direct payload loads at lateral ends of the at least one cargo support segment to the at least one rail via at least one medially located interface region of the fixed central region configured to contact the at least one rail in the second arrangement.
52. (New) The system of claim 51, wherein the interface region spans along at least a portion of a length of the at least one cargo support segment.
53. (New) The system of claim 51, wherein the interface region of the at least one cargo support segment, in the first arrangement, is spaced apart from the at least one rail.
54. (New) The system of claim 50, further comprising a transition mechanism configured to switch the at least one cargo support segment between the first arrangement and the second arrangement.
55. (New) The system of claim 50, wherein the at least one cargo support segment comprises a fixation mechanism configured to fixedly secure the at least one cargo support segment with respect to the location along the length of the at least one rail by creating a geometric interference between the at least one cargo support segment and at least one of the at least one rail or other structural element of the cargo aircraft, the geometric interference being configured to prevent movement of the at least one cargo support segment with respect to the at least one rail.
56. (New) The system of claim 55, wherein the fixation mechanism comprises a locking body configured to pass through an opening associated with the at least one rail or the other structural element of the cargo aircraft to create the geometric interference.
57. (New) The system of The system of wherein at least one cargo support segment is configured to be securely fixed at one or more predetermined locations along the at least one rail, and
wherein the opposing lateral end segments are sized and shaped to correspond to an inner surface of the cargo bay at the one or more predetermined locations in the second position.
58. (New) A removable cargo bay support system for a cargo aircraft, comprising:at least one rail disposed in an interior cargo bay of a cargo aircraft, the interior cargo bay having a forward bay portion located in a forward end of the cargo aircraft, an aft bay portion located in an aft end of the cargo aircraft, and the at least one rail extending longitudinally along a length of the forward bay portion and a length of the aft bay portion; and
at least one cargo support segment configured to be removably attached to the at least one
rail, and, when attached to the at least one rail, the at least one cargo support segment is transformable between a first arrangement in which the at least one cargo support segment is translatable along a length of the at least one rail, and a second arrangement in which the at least one cargo support segment is fixedly secured with respect to a location along the length of the at least one rail,wherein the at least one cargo support segment is configured to support cargo weight and direct at least a majority of the cargo weight supported by the at least one cargo support segment into the at least one rail, and
wherein the at least one cargo support segment comprises one or more lateral support beams configured to direct payload loads at lateral ends of the at least one cargo support segment to the at least one rail via a medially located interface region configured to contact the at least one rail in the second arrangement
59. (New) The system of claim 58, wherein the at least one cargo support segment is configured to, when fixedly secured with respect to a location along the length of the at least one rail, define a section of a floor of the cargo bay of the cargo aircraft 60. (New) A method of loading a cargo support onto a cargo aircraft, comprising:removably attaching at least one cargo support segment to one or more rails disposed in an interior cargo bay of a cargo aircraft, the interior cargo bay having a forward bay portion located in a forward end of the cargo aircraft, an aft bay portion located in an aft end of the cargo aircraft, and the one or more rails extending longitudinally along a length of the forward bay portion and a length of the aft bay portion, the at least one cargo support segment comprising a fixed central region and opposing lateral end segments moveably coupled to the fixed region and moveable between a first position and a second position, the first position defining a first width of the at least one cargo support segment that is less than a second width of the at least one cargo support segment in the second position;
translating the at least one cargo support segment along the one or more rails in the first position and through at least a portion of the interior cargo bay to a desired location along a length of the one or more rails, a location along the portion of the interior cargo bay defining a width along the one or more rails that is less than the second width of the at least one cargo support segment and less than a nominal width of the interior cargo bay along the one or more
rails at the desired location;moving the lateral end segments of the at least one cargo support segment to the second position, and
fixedly securing the at least one cargo support segment in the second position at the desired location to define a section of a cargo support of the cargo bay of the cargo aircraft.
61. (New) The method of claim 60, wherein the at least one cargo support segment comprises a plurality of cargo support segments, the method further comprising:sequentially attaching the plurality of cargo support segments to the one or more rails,
translating each cargo support segment of the plurality of cargo support segments to respective desired locations, each desired location being corresponding adjacent locations to each other; and
fixedly securing each cargo support segment of the plurality of cargo support segments at the respective desired locations to define a continuous section of the cargo support of the cargo bay.
62. (New) The method of claim 61, further comprising attaching each cargo support segment of the plurality of cargo support segments to an adj acent cargo support segment of the plurality of cargo support segments.
63. (New) The method of claim 60, wherein fixedly securing the at least one cargo support segment further comprises contacting the one or more rails with an interface region of the at least one cargo support segment, the interface region spanning along at least a portion of a length of the at least one cargo support segment.
64. (New) The method of claim 63, wherein the interface region is spaced apart from the one or more rails when translating the at least one cargo support segment along the one or more rails.
65. (New) The method of claim 63, wherein fixedly securing the at least one cargo support segment further comprises at least one of raising or lowering the interface region with respect to the one or more rails.
66. (New) The method of claim 65, wherein a transition mechanism of at least one cargo support segment switches the at least one cargo support segment between a first arrangement in
which the at least one cargo support segment can be advanced along the one or more rails and a second arrangement in which movement of the at least one cargo support segment along the one or more rails is resisted by the interface region.
67. (New) The method of claim 60, wherein fixedly securing the at least one cargo support segment further comprises creating a geometric interference between the at least one cargo support segment and at least one of the one or more rails or other structural element of the cargo aircraft.
68. (New) The method of claim 67, wherein creating the geometric interference comprises disposing a locking body coupled to the at least one cargo support segment through an opening associated with the one or more rails or the other structural element of the cargo aircraft.
